title: Set up a GenAI prompt
summary: put a one-click AI command on the sales order line form that says whether the line has shipped, and prove its answer against what LN shows.

phases.title: Confirm a model is available
phases.route: Tools ➔ Application Extensibility ➔ Embedded GenAI ➔ GenAI LLMs

tokens.v: LN has no language model of its own. It keeps a list retrieved from the Infor GenAI application, and that service marks one model and one version of it as the default. A prompt that names no model uses the default, so this phase is a look and not a setting.

phases.title: Model the dataset
phases.route: Tools ➔ Application Extensibility ➔ Embedded GenAI ➔ Datasets

tokens.v: A dataset is the LN data that will travel with the question, and it is the whole of what the model is told. It starts from one main table, which has to be the table of the screen the command will sit on, because the record the user has open reaches the dataset through its selection index. Fields of related tables can be added beneath it. Every field ticked is sent, so tick only what the prompt will name.

phases.title: Write the prompt
phases.route: Tools ➔ Application Extensibility ➔ Embedded GenAI ➔ GenAI Prompts

tokens.v: A prompt row ties a label, a dataset and two texts together. The label's description becomes the command's name. The instruction text is shown to the user beside the answer. The prompt text is what is sent to the model, with the dataset's output put where its data marker stands. The model fields can stay blank, and then the service's default answers.

tokens.v: Nothing shows on any screen until a prompt is linked to a session code. The link is to one exact code: the command appears on that session and on no other, however alike two screens look. Three settings on the link decide whether the command is offered, to whom, and with what selected.

phases.title: Run it and check the answer

tokens.v: When the command is chosen, LN runs the dataset for the line on the form, writes the result into the prompt text and sends it to the model. The answer opens in a window of its own. The model answers only from what the dataset sent, and a wrong answer looks the same as a right one, so the first runs are checked against the form, once for each kind of line the prompt can meet.
